rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being granted respite is not an honor; God sent Moses to Pharaoh and Haman to establish proof despite their hostility, while addressing Iblis itself honors him.
rows.anchor: مجرد الإرسال ليس بتشريف وإنما يكون لإقامة الحجة بدلالة أن موسى عليه السلام أرسله الله إلى فرعون وهامان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The calling in “And the day He calls them” is performed through some of the angels.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى : {ويوم يناديهم} (القصص : 62) أي : على لسان بعض ملائكته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prefixed bāʾ in Iblis’s oath is governed by an omitted verb of swearing.
rows.anchor: الباء متعلقة بفعل القسم المحذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ighwāʾ means leading astray from the upright way; the hamza marks becoming, so Iblis blames God for making him stray from guidance and mercy because of Adam’s descendants.
rows.anchor: والإغواء الإضلال عن المنهج القويم ، والهمزة فيه للصيرورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis means that he will lie in wait for Adam and his descendants, like highway robbers ambushing travelers.
rows.anchor: لآدم وذريته ترصدا بهم كما يقعد القطاع للقطع على السابلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The straight path is Islam, leading to Paradise; sitting on it metaphorically means exerting oneself to mislead humanity with single-minded effort.
rows.anchor: صراطك} أي : على صراطك {المستقيم} الموصل إلى الجنة وهو دين الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heights are the elevated tops of the barrier separating the two abodes; elevation makes them more recognizable than lower ground.
rows.anchor: أي : أعراف ذلك الحجاب ، أي أعاليه وهو السور المضروب بينها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view identifies the barrier’s heights with Mount Uhud; ʿurf means any high, elevated place, like a rooster’s or horse’s crest.
rows.anchor: قيل هو جبل أحد يوضع هناك جمع عرف وهو كل عال مرتفع ومنه عرف الديك والفرس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view identifies the people of the heights as believers whose good and bad deeds are equal, leaving them between Paradise and Hell until they prostrate; the act tips their scale toward Paradise.
rows.anchor: طائفة من المؤمنين تساوت حسناتهم وسيئاتهم فهم ينظرون إلى النار وينظرون إلى الجنة ومالهم رجحان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before entry, the people of both abodes are recognized by God-given signs such as white or black faces; after entry, sight makes inference from signs unnecessary.
rows.anchor: بسبب علاماتهم التي أعلمهم الله كبياض الوجه وسواده وهذا في العرصات قبل دخول الجنة والنار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The calling, turning, and bringing mentioned here take place after entry into Paradise and Hell.
rows.anchor: وأما النداء والصرف والإتيان فبعد الدخول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The men are the subject of “they called”; the past tense portrays the call as already realized, and the phrase is a second description of the men.
rows.anchor: أي : الرجال وهو صفة ثانية لرجال عدل إلى لفظ الماضي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the men look toward Paradise’s inhabitants, they greet them with an honorific greeting and announce safety from every hardship.
rows.anchor: إذا نظروا إليهم سلموا عليهم سلام التحية والإكرام وبشروهم بالسلامة من جميع المكاره والآفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After settling in their abodes, the people of Hell call the people of Paradise; they have been allowed to see their relatives there, although the relatives do not recognize their blackened faces.
rows.anchor: وذلك أنهم لما بقوا فيها جياعا عطاشا ، قالوا : يا ربنا إن لنا قرابات في الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They ask for Paradise’s water to cool their thirst and the heat they suffer.
rows.anchor: أي صبوا {من المآء} أي : ماء الجنة حتى يطفىء عنا حر ما نجد من العطش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their alternative request may be for other drinks or food to ease hunger; if food is intended, it suits the sense of giving abundantly.
rows.anchor: {أو مما رزقكم الله} من سائر الأشربة ليلائم الإفاضة

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan prefers understanding afīḍū as “cast” or “throw.”
rows.anchor: قال أبو حيان : الصحيح تضمين أفيضوا معنى ألقوا

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan says they were worldly slaves of appetite and died as they had lived, while Paradise’s inhabitants had endured hunger for the feast of Paradise.
rows.anchor: وهؤلاء القائلون كانوا في الدنيا عبيد البطون حريصين على الطعام والشراب حتى ماتوا على ما عاشوا فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse shows that people still need food and drink even while being punished.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية : بيان أن الإنسان لا يستغني عن الطعام والشراب وإن كان في العذاب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas answers that water is the best charity, citing Hell’s inhabitants begging the people of Paradise for it.
rows.anchor: قال أبو الجوزاء : سألت ابن عباس رضي الله عنهم أي الصدقة أفضل قال الماء

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: When Saʿd ibn ʿUbāda asked about charity for his deceased mother, the Prophet named water; Saʿd dug a well for her, supporting the benefit of charity for the dead.
rows.anchor: وعن سعد بن عبادة أنه قال يا رسول الله إن أم سعد ماتت ، فأي صدقة أفضل قال عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Water is singled out either because the Ḥijāz needs it greatly, increasing its reward, or because its coolness counters Hell’s heat.
rows.anchor: يقول الفقير في الحديث دلالة على نفع الصدقة في الأموات كما ذهب إليه أهل السنة ، وتخصيص الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Paradise’s inhabitants are not permitted to answer for forty years, after which they reply to the people of Hell.
rows.anchor: روي أنه لا يؤذن لأهل الجنة في الجواب مقدار أربعين سنة ثم يؤذن لهم في جوابهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has barred the food and drink of Paradise from unbelievers; their drink is boiling water and their food is dariʿ and zaqqum.
rows.anchor: أي : منع طعام الجنة وشرابها عنهم منع المحرم عن المكلف فلا سبيل إلى ذلك قطعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Their religion” is the religion they were commanded to follow, Islam.
rows.anchor: الذي أمروا بالتدين به وهو دين الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They turned religion into amusement by making whatever they wished forbidden or lawful and following desires adorned by Satan instead of God’s command.
rows.anchor: يتلاعبون به يحرمون ما شاؤوا ويحلون ما شاؤوا ولا يتبعون أمر الله تعالى وإنما يتبعون أهواءهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view says their original religion was that of Ismail, which they altered to whatever they wanted.
rows.anchor: وقيل : كان دينهم دين إسماعيل عليه السلام فغيروه وتدينوا بما شاؤوا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view takes the phrase to mean that they devoted themselves to unsuitable pursuits and sought enjoyment in what should not be sought.
rows.anchor: أو صرفوا همتهم فيما لا ينبغي أن تصرف إليه الهمم وطلبوا أن يفرحوا بما لا ينبغي أن يطلب

rows.speaker: التفسير الفارسي
rows.claim: The Persian commentary glosses the phrase as their feast, when they went around the Kaaba clapping and playing.
rows.anchor: وفي "التفسير الفارسي" : {دينهم} (عيد خودرا) {لهوا ولعبا} مشغول وبازيه ايشان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Eid play with weapons, riding, and races on horseback or foot is permitted; early drums had no jingles, while current mizmar and jingling drums at celebrations are unlicensed amusement.
rows.anchor: ويرخص اللعب في يوم العيد بالسلاح والركض ، أي التسابق بالأفراس والأرجل وغير ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A claim that religion allows latitude applies only to permitted matters; joking is lawful only when it does not violate religious law.
rows.anchor: وقولهم إن في ديننا فسحة إنما هو بالنسبة إلى الأمور المرخصة ألا يرى أن المزاج مباح إذا كان بما لا يخالف الشرع

rows.speaker: أبو بكر
rows.claim: The report says Abu Jahl sent a mocker to ask the Prophet for grapes or fruit from his Paradise, and Abu Bakr replied that God forbids both to unbelievers.
rows.anchor: كما روي في الخبر أن أبا جهل بعث إلى النبي عليه السلام رجلا يستهزىء به أن أطعمني من عنب جنتك أو شيئا من الفواكه فقال أبو بكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Persian poem warns the wise not to be distracted by the world’s deceptive colors and changing warmth or cold, but to guard themselves from its deceit.
rows.anchor: درديده اعتبار خوابيست بر رهكذر اجل سرابيست مشغول مشو بسرخ وزردش انديشه مكن زكرم وسردش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Today” means the Day of Resurrection, and the prefixed fa introduces the consequence.
rows.anchor: {فاليوم} أي : يوم القيامة والفاء فصيحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will treat them like someone utterly disregarded and left behind in Hell; this is figurative, since God is transcendent above literal forgetfulness.
rows.anchor: نفعل بهم ما يفعل الناسي بالمنسي من عدم الاعتداد بهم ، وتركهم في النار تركا كليا شبه معاملته تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison means they failed to keep the meeting of this Day in mind or prepare for it; they could not literally forget what they never acknowledged, so the unseen is conveyed through a familiar analogy.
rows.anchor: وإن لم يصح وصفهم بنسيانه حقيقة لأن النسيان يكون بعد المعرفة وهم لم يكونوا معترفين بلقاء يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their continuing denial that the signs came from God is coordinated with their neglect; the particle mā is infinitival, and the comparison in kamā is causal through the implication of abandonment.
rows.anchor: عطف على ما نسوا ، أي وكما كانوا منكرين بأنها من عند الله إنكارا مستمرا فما مصدرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The detailed Book explains doctrines, rulings, and admonitions; the referent may be all unbelievers, with “Book” generic, or the contemporaries, with the Book being the Quran.
rows.anchor: بيناه معانيه من العقائد والأحكام والمواعظ مفصلة والضمير للكفرة قاطبة والمراد بالكتاب الجنس أو للمعاصرين منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “With knowledge” can describe the explainer as knowing how to detail the Book wisely, or the Book as containing many wisdoms.
rows.anchor: حال من فاعل فصلناه أي عالمين بوجه تفصيله حتى جاء حكيما أو من مفعوله أي مشتملا على حكم كثيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Book is guidance and mercy for believers because they affirm it comes from God and benefit from its effects and lights.
rows.anchor: {هدى ورحمة} حال من هاء فصلناه أي حال كون ذلك الكتاب هاديا وذا رحمة {لقوم يؤمنون}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unbelievers await only the Book’s eventual fulfillment, when the truth of its promised reward and threat becomes evident.
rows.anchor: ما ينتظر هؤلاء الكفرة بعدم إيمانهم به إلا ما يؤول إليه أمره من تبين صدقه بظهور ما أخبر به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bushran is a shortened form of bushur, plural of bashīr, meaning bearers of glad tidings.
rows.anchor: تخفيف بشر بضمتين جمع بشير نحو رغيف ورغف ، أي : مبشرات.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The winds precede the rain: the east wind raises clouds, the north gathers them, the south drives rain from them, and the west disperses them; their directional names are explained.
rows.anchor: فإن الصبا تثير السحاب والشمال تجمعه والجنوب تدره والدبور

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas compares God’s winds carrying and working the clouds until rain falls to a man milking a she-camel or sheep.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : يرسل الله الرياح فتحمل السحاب فتمريه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse uses “mercy” to mean rain, so a saying about fleeing from mercy refers to fleeing from rain.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية إطلاق الرحمة على المطر ، فقول : من قال إني أفر من الرحمة محمول على المطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “until it carries” marks the endpoint of the statement that God sends the winds.
rows.anchor: {حتى إذآ أقلت} غاية لقوله : يرسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aqallat means the wind carried the cloud easily; carrying something with ease makes it seem light, hence its derivation from the sense of fewness.
rows.anchor: أي : حملته ورفعته باليسر والسهولة بأن وجدته خفيفا قليلا يقال أقللت كذا ، أي : حملته بالسهولة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Heavy” describes clouds laden with water; sahāb is a collective noun that can denote one cloud or many, so the adjective is plural in sense.
rows.anchor: جمع ثقيل أي بالماء جمعه مع كونه وصفا للسحاب ، لأن السحاب اسم جنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sahāb means clouds moving through the sky.
rows.anchor: والسحاب : هو الغيم الجاري في السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sūqnāhu derives from driving; the pronoun refers to the clouds, singular in form to match the word’s grammatical form.
rows.anchor: من السوق والضمير للسحاب والإفراد باعتبار اللفظ والمعنى بالفارسية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A dead land is a place without vegetation; balad can mean any inhabited or uninhabited location, while balda is a part of it and bilād its plural.
rows.anchor: {لبلد ميت} أي : لإحياء بلد لا نبات فيه والبلد يطلق على كل موضع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to the land, and the bāʾ marks water adhering to or being sent upon it.
rows.anchor: {فأنزلنا به المآء} أي : بالبلد والباء للإلصاق أي التصق إنزال الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next bāʾ means “by means of” that water; “all fruits” refers to every kind, with universality understood in the customary sense.
rows.anchor: {فأخرجنا به} أي : بسبب ذلك الماء {من كل الثمرات} أي : من كل أنواعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Resurrection is likened either to producing fruits or to reviving dead land: God will return souls to gathered bodily matter and restore powers and senses.
rows.anchor: الإشارة فيه إلى إخراج الثمرات أو إلى إحياء البلد الميت أي كما نحييه بإحداث القوة النباتية فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The form tadhakkarūn drops one of two tāʾs and means “you remember,” teaching that the One who can do this can raise the dead without doubt.
rows.anchor: {لعلكم تذكرون} بطرح إحدى التاءين ، أي تتذكرون فتعلمون

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وأبو هريرة
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Abu Hurayra report that rain falls for forty days between the two blasts, bodies grow from graves as plants grow from water, receive souls, then awaken at the blast of resurrection.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس وأبو هريرة : إذا مات الناس كلهم في النفخة الأولى مطرت السماء أربعين يوما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the inward reading, winds are care, cloud is guidance, water is love, and its fruits are visions, unveilings, and spiritual perfections; God raises dead hearts from the graves of breasts.
rows.anchor: والإشارة في الآية : أن الرياح رياح العناية ، والسحاب سحاب الهداية ، والماء ماء المحبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lesson recalls the life of intimacy and nearness in the holy precincts.
rows.anchor: أي موتى القلوب من قبور الصدور لعلكم تذكرون ، أي : تذكرون أيام حياتكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Primordial divine care is the foundation and reaches servants in public and private; a story begins of a saint sent among polytheists, captured, and serving at a church faithfully.
rows.anchor: واعلم : أن العمدة هي العناية الأزلية ، وهي تصل إلى العباد في الخلا والملا حكي أنه قيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story continues that the saint was sold to a church servant, served honestly, then appeared to a sultan who had emptied the church to pray and answered that he was a Muslim like him.
rows.anchor: فأسره مشرك وباعه لخادم كنيسة فخدم فيها زمانا بالصدق ، فجاء السلطان يوما إلى الكنيسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The council says Moses will corrupt the people’s religion in Egypt and turn them away from following Pharaoh.
rows.anchor: يفسدوا على الناس دينهم في أرض مصر ويصرفوهم عن متابعتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The coordinated phrase “and your gods” means Pharaoh’s objects of worship.
rows.anchor: {ويذرك} عطف على يفسدوا {وءالهتك} معبوداتك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view says Pharaoh worshipped the stars; the author prefers the Persian commentary’s account that he made idols in his own image and ordered worship of them as a route to him.
rows.anchor: قيل : كان يعبد الكواكب والأصح كما في "التفسير الفارسي" أنه صنع لقومه أصناما على صورته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh threatens to resume killing Israelite sons and keeping their daughters alive as servants, as he did around Moses’s birth, to show his rule remains dominant and dispel the prediction that a boy would end it.
rows.anchor: والمقصود سنعود إلى قتل أبنائهم واستخدام نسائهم كما كنا نفعل وقت ولادة موسى ليعلم أنا على ما كنا عليه من القهر والغلبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “We are dominant over them” means Pharaoh’s force still subdues them under his control, unchanged from before.
rows.anchor: أي : مستعلون عليهم بالقوة كما كنا لم يتغير حالنا أصلا ، وهم مقهورون تحت أيدينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses comforts his people and promises a good outcome after hearing Pharaoh’s threat and seeing their helplessness.
rows.anchor: تسلية لهم وعدة لحسن العاقبة حين سمعوا قول فرعون وعجزوا عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He tells them to seek God’s aid and endure Pharaoh’s false words.
rows.anchor: {واصبروا} على ما سمعتم من أقاويله الباطلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The land” here means Egypt, which God gives as an inheritance to whichever servants He wills.
rows.anchor: {إن الارض} أي أرض مصر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The good outcome means victory and triumph or Paradise, and belongs to the God-fearing; the Israelites are among them.
rows.anchor: {للمتقين} الذين أنتم منهم ؛ لأنه روي أنه لما غلب سحرة فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Moses’s proof prevailed over Pharaoh’s magicians, six hundred thousand Israelites believed and avoided associating partners with God and disobedience.
rows.anchor: لما غلب سحرة فرعون وتبين نبوة موسى بسطوع حجته آمن بموسى من بني إسرائيل ستمائة ألف نفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse implies that seeking God’s help and patience are forms of God-consciousness.
rows.anchor: وفيه إيذان بأن الاستعانة بالله تعالى والصبر من باب التقوى

rows.speaker: الحافظ
rows.claim: Hafez’s poem presents patience in the grief-filled hut as the reward for being honored by the companion of Joseph’s face.
rows.anchor:
قال الحافظ :
آنكه يرانه سرم صحبت يوف بنواخت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following “they said” refers to the Israelites.
rows.anchor: {قالوا} أي : بنو إسرائيل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses returned from Mount Sinai intensely angry; the word asaf means anger, as in “when they angered Us.” God had informed him during the conversation that his people worshipped the calf.
rows.anchor: حال كونه {غضبان أسفا} أي : شديد الغضب يقال آسفني فأسفت أي : أغضبني فغضبت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “You acted badly in my absence” condemns their conduct while Moses was away; mā is an indefinite descriptive noun explaining the implicit subject of biʾsa, with the condemned succession understood.
rows.anchor: ساء ما عملتم خلفي أيها العبدة بعد غيبتي وانطلاقي إلى الجبل لأنه يقال خلفه بما يكره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative hamza rebukes them: they abandoned the Lord’s command before its proper completion, namely waiting faithfully for Moses and keeping his covenant.
rows.anchor: الهمزة للإنكار أي أتركتموه غير تام كأنه ضمن عجل معنى سبق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here the command can mean the commandments or what was commanded; haste is acting before its time and is blameworthy, unlike speed at the beginning of the proper time.
rows.anchor: فالأمر واحد الأوامر أو أنه بمعنى المأمور به ، والعجلة : العمل بالشيء قبل وقته ولذلك صارت مذمومة بخلاف السرعة

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The inward reading addresses the spirit’s qualities: they hastened back to worldly adornment and attachment before God’s command, interrupting the spiritual journey.
rows.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : استعجلتم يا صفات الروح بالرجوع إلى الدنيا وزينتها والتعلق بها

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Seekers and attendants of kings should turn from worldly things during the spiritual path; only after crossing the ego’s and desire’s wastes may they return to guide people to God.
rows.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى أن أرباب الطلب ، وأصحاب الملوك لا ينبغي أن يلتفتوا إلى شيء من الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses threw down the tablets of the Torah and pulled Aaron by the hair toward himself in reproach, not to humiliate him, supposing he had failed to restrain the people; Aaron was older, gentle, and loved by the Israelites.
rows.anchor: وألقى الالواح} التي كانت فيها التوراة من يده.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Son of my mother” omits the vocative particle and its substitute alif for ease; although full brothers, Aaron names their mother to soften Moses and invite compassion, as Arabic custom does.
rows.anchor: {ابن أم} بحذف حرف النداء ، وأصله يا ابن أما حذفت الألف المبدلة من الياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aaron says the people overpowered him and nearly killed him to dispel Moses’s suspicion that he had been negligent: he had tried his utmost to stop them.
rows.anchor: إزاحة لتوهم التقصير في حقه ، والمعنى : بذلت وسعي في كفهم حتى قهروني واستضعفوني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aaron asks Moses not to do anything that gives enemies cause to rejoice over him; the word denotes delight at an enemy’s misfortune, and such gloating is worse than any hardship.
rows.anchor: {فلا تشمت بى الاعدآء} أي : فلا تفعل بي ما يكون سببا لشماتتهم بي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aaron asks not to be counted among the wrongdoers through punishment or accusation of failure.
rows.anchor: {ولا تجعلنى مع القوم الظالمين} أي : معدودا في عدادهم بالمؤاخذة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the inward reading, Aaron is the heart, Moses the spirit, and their enemies the ego, Satan, and desire; the wrongdoers are heart’s qualities that worship the calf of the world.
rows.anchor: أن هارون القلب أخ موسى الروح والأعداء النفس والشيطان والهوى والقوم الظالمون هم الذين عبدوا عجل الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heart itself remains naturally oriented to loving and seeking God, though its qualities can take on the ego’s vices; the ego remains oriented to worldly desire while its qualities pass through spiritual states.
rows.anchor: ولكن القلب من حيث هو هو لا يتغير عما جبل عليه من محبة الله وطلبه وإنما تتغير صفاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If left to itself even briefly, the ego returns to its original nature; God’s established law does not change.
rows.anchor: ولو وكلت إلى نفسها طرفة عين لعادت المشومة إلى طبعها وجبلتها سنة الله التي قد خلت من قبل ولن تجد لسنة الله تبديلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses asks forgiveness for himself for how he treated Aaron and for Aaron if he failed to restrain them; he asks for himself to reassure Aaron and silence gloaters, and for Aaron to acknowledge his need for forgiveness.
rows.anchor: {رب اغفر لى} أي : ما فعلت بأخي من غير ذنب مقرر من قبله {ولاخى} أي : أن فرط في كفهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Admission into God’s mercy asks for further favor after forgiveness; al-Haddādī glosses it as admission to Paradise.
rows.anchor: بمزيد الأنعام علينا بعد غفران ما سلف منا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is more merciful to Moses and Aaron than they are to themselves or than their parents are to them.
rows.anchor: وأنت أرحم بنا منا على أنفسنا ومن آبائنا وأمهاتنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A story tells of a dying boy unable to utter the testimony until his mother forgave him after the Prophet threatened to burn him for having blinded her; her recollection of bearing and nursing him moved her to pardon him.
rows.anchor: حكي أنه اعتقل لسان فتى عن الشهادة حين أشرف على الموت فأخبروا النبي عليه السلام فدخل عليه وعرض الشهادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story contrasts a mother’s limited mercy, which would not permit burning her son, with God’s greater mercy toward a believer who has held the testimony for seventy years.
rows.anchor: فالله الذي لا يتضرر بجناية العباد كيف يستجيز إحراق المؤمن المواظب على كلمة الشهادة سبعين سنة وهو أرحم الراحمين

rows.speaker: الحافظ
rows.claim: Hafez says God’s kindness exceeds human sin and bids the heart trust the Friend’s boundless mercy.
rows.anchor:
قال الحافظ :
لطف خدا بيشتر ازجرم ماست

rows.speaker: بعض أهل التفسير
rows.claim: Some exegetes recount that Cain invoked God’s mercy and the name Muhammad to escape being swallowed by the earth after killing Abel and challenging God about spared sinners.
rows.anchor: قال بعض أهل التفسير : إن قابيل لما قتل أخاه هابيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If God showed this degree of mercy to an unbeliever, a sinner should seek forgiveness for hidden and manifest faults to enter the highest Paradise.
rows.anchor: فاعتبر إذا كانت رحمته بهذه المرتبة للكافر فما ظنك للمؤمن فينبغي للمقصر أن يرفع حاجته إلى المولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author quotes Hafez confessing that he sees no one with a darker record than himself.
rows.anchor: سياه نامه ترازخود كسى نمى بينم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inward reading treats “forgive me and my brother” as a journey through divine attributes: the spirit and heart are ready for the divine attraction that brings them into that realm.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله تعالى : {رب اغفر لى} الآية إشارة إلى السير في الصفات

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: God alone can bring another into His attributes, as shown by the verse that He admits whom He wills into His mercy.
rows.anchor: قوله : {يدخل من يشآء فى رحمته} (الشورى : 8) كذا في "التأويلات النجمية".

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The calf worshippers, including the Samaritan and his followers, will face great punishment in the afterlife for an exceptionally grave sin; divine wrath here means its outcome, vengeance and torment, since literal anger does not apply to God.
rows.anchor: أي : في الآخرة {غضب} عظيم كائن {من ربهم} أي : مالكهم لما أن جريمتم أعظم الجرائم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their humiliation includes exile and abasement for them and their descendants; the Samaritan was isolated and forbidden contact, a condition said to persist among his descendants.
rows.anchor: هي ذلة الاغتراب والمسكنة المنتظمة لهم ولأولادهم والذلة التي اختص بها السامري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Moses intended to kill the Samaritan, but God told him to expel him because he was generous; Moses ordered him to live apart, saying no one could touch him or be touched by him.
rows.anchor: كما روي أن موسى عليه السلام هم بقتل السامري ، فأوحى الله إليه لا تقتل السامري فإنه سخي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The future marker is used with an event already past by letting the descendants’ later condition represent the forebears’ condition.
rows.anchor: وإيراد ما نالهم في حيز السين مع مضيه بطريق تغليب حال الأخلاف على حال الأسلاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The forgers are punished; no fabrication is greater than their claim that the calf was the god of both Israel and Moses, a claim the author says no one else ever made.
rows.anchor: على الله ولا فرية أعظم من فريتهم هذا إلهكم وإله موسى ولعله لم يفتر مثلها أحد قبلهم ولا بعدهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise includes anyone who committed any kind of sin, then repented and believed with sincere faith, acted righteously, and did not persist like the first group.
rows.anchor: {والذين عملوا السياات} أية سيئة كانت {ثم تابوا} من تلك السيئات.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Thereafter” refers to after repentance joined with faith; God forgives sins regardless of their magnitude or number and abundantly grants mercy in this world and the next.
rows.anchor: المقرونة بالإيمان {لغفور} للذنوب وإن عظمت وكثرت {رحيم} مبالغ في إفاضة فنون الرحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the inward reading, the calf is the idol of caprice, as supported by the verse about taking one’s desire as a god; serving desire brings divine wrath and worldly humiliation.
rows.anchor: عجل الهوى إلها يدل عليه قوله : {أفرءيت من اتخذ إلاهه هوااه} (الجاثية : 23)

rows.speaker: النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام
rows.claim: The Prophet says nothing worshipped on earth is more hateful to God than caprice.
rows.anchor: قول النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام : "ما عبد في الأرض إله أبغض على الله من الهوى"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The servant of caprice is humbled by bodily desires and captive to bestial, predatory, and satanic traits while attached to worldly life.
rows.anchor: وإن عابد الهوى يكون ذليل شهوات النفس وأسير صفاتها الذميمة من الحيوانية والسبعية والشيطانية ما دام يميل إلى الحياة الدنيوية
